title: Spring Boot: The Power of IoC

scenes.say: Who really controls your app? Is it you, or Spring? Let's see why this matters for every Spring Boot project.

scenes.label: IoC
scenes.sub: Spring manages objects and wiring, not your code.
scenes.say: The core of Spring is Inversion of Control. That means Spring, not you, creates and wires up your objects.

Here's how it works. You write a bean, just a regular Java class. Spring injects what it needs, using constructor or field injection. It also controls the bean's lifecycle. Most beans are singletons by default.
For example, with REST, you just add a Rest Controller annotation. Spring handles the rest—no need to wire up endpoints yourself.

scenes.label: Auto-Config
scenes.sub: Boot auto-configures beans from your classpath.
scenes.say: Spring Boot takes this further. It auto-configures beans based on what's on your classpath, so you skip the boilerplate.

scenes.question: What happens if a bean calls its own @Transactional method?
scenes.right: Self-invocation skips the proxy, so @Transactional is ignored. Move the method to another bean.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap. If a bean calls its own transactional method, the transaction won't work. Spring's proxy gets skipped. To fix it, move that method to another bean.
